title: Minimize the Maximum Waiting Time at Synchronized Traffic Lights
summary: Given an integer period and an array lights, where lights[i] represents the duration of the green phase for the i-th traffic light, and an array arrivalTime indicating the arrival time of each car, assign each car to exactly one traffic light.
statement: Given an integer period and an array lights, where lights[i] represents the duration of the green phase for the i-th traffic light, and an array arrivalTime indicating the arrival time of each car, assign each car to exactly one traffic light. The penalty is defined as the maximum waiting time among all cars. The waiting time for a car j assigned to the i-th traffic light is 0 if arrivalTime[j] % period is less than lights[i], and period - (arrivalTime[j] % period) otherwise. Return the minimum possible penalty.
constraints: A light with green length g gives zero wait when arrival mod period < g, otherwise period-remainder.
Assign each car independently to one light.
Minimize the maximum waiting time across all cars.
hints: Only the longest green phase can weakly improve any car’s wait.
When the remainder is outside that phase, its wait is period-remainder.
Take the maximum of these individually minimized waits.
editorial: Take the maximum of these individually minimized waits.

tests.explanation: The longest green phase is three; waits are zero, three, zero, and five, so the maximum is five.
A full-period green phase gives every car zero wait.
